sample_unit: LLM responses to bee sting questions (25 questions x 3 models)

links.outcome: Readability of LLM responses versus sixth-grade reading level standard
links.effect: No model met the sixth-grade reading level standard; all models had excessively high readability levels.
links.quote: No model met the sixth-grade reading level standard.

links.outcome: Readability of LLM patient information responses across six readability indices
links.effect: No model met the sixth-grade reading level standard; all had excessively high readability levels. Doubao ranked highest on understandability (PEMAT-U 73.00%).
links.quote: No model met the sixth-grade reading level standard.

links.outcome: Frequency of outdated medical advice among LLM content deficits
links.effect: Eleven content deficits identified; outdated medical advice was most common (45.45%), followed by omissions (36.36%) and hallucinations (18.18%).
links.quote: Eleven content deficits were identified: outdated medical advice (45.45%), omissions (36.36%), and hallucinations (18.18%).

screen.reason: Empirical evaluation of three LLMs answering patient questions about bee stings, evaluated by emergency physicians for quality/safety and patients for comprehensibility/credibility, but does not test a specific deployment safeguard or practice.
